title: sse: fix streaming chunking/framing for partial-JSON and delimiter ordering
author: Maya Patel
description:
Context: We observed multiple customer reports and internal e2e tests where SSE streaming from the OpenAI-compat and native SSE endpoints emitted delimiter tokens (newline/data markers) in the wrong order relative to partial JSON fragments. Symptoms included: partial JSON objects split across SSE events being emitted with delimiter markers that caused clients to see malformed chunks (e.g. trailing commas, stray `]` tokens) or the special [DONE] event arriving before buffered fragments were flushed.

Motivation: This affects streaming stability for function/tool calling and structured output use cases where consumers parse incremental JSON (partial objects/arrays). The root cause is twofold: 1) the framer inserted stream delimiters based on token boundaries rather than JSON structural boundaries, and 2) the buffer flush logic allowed out-of-order emission when an asynchronous codec callback completed after a delimiter was queued.

What this PR does:
- Reworks the SSE framer to track top-level JSON tokens (objects/arrays/commas) and only emit delimiter/event boundaries between top-level elements, not between arbitrary token fragments.
- Adds a small state machine to the streaming runtime to ensure flush ordering: the delimiter/event marker is emitted after the buffered fragment is fully serialized and acknowledged by the codec, preventing the [DONE] event from winning races.
- Improves test coverage: deterministic unit tests for delimiter ordering, fuzz-style chunk boundary tests, and an integration test exercising the OpenAI-compat streaming path (including function call streaming).
- Adds a compatibility shim to openai_compat to normalize cases where legacy clients expect a trailing newline before [DONE]. The shim is opt-in and used only for routes labeled legacy-openai-compat.

Checklist:
- [x] Reproduce with unit/integration tests
- [x] Add deterministic tests for ordering and partial JSON cases
- [x] Ensure OpenAI-compat behaviour remains backward-compatible (config-gated)

release_notes: Fixes SSE streaming framing and delimiter ordering for partial-JSON streams. Improves stability for incremental JSON parsing (function/tool calling, structured output). Backwards-compatible shim for legacy OpenAI-compat clients available via config flag.
notes_for_ops: Operators should be aware of the new config flag openai_compat.legacy_newline_shim (default false). Enabling restores legacy newline-before-[DONE] behavior for a small subset of routes; prefer leaving default off. No infra changes required.
follow_up: Track ENG-4189 to evaluate whether additional heuristics (semantic-aware chunking for large arrays) are needed for extreme tokenization patterns. Also monitor relevant SLOs for streaming p99 latency for one week after rollout.
examples_and_repro: Repro script: tests/integration/streaming_repro.sh simulates chunk boundaries and verifies event order
Manual repro: curl --no-buffer to the /v1/stream endpoint with a model that emits large JSON arrays; observe delimiter ordering and use --raw to see SSE framing
